# Pagination

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use pagination to help users move through a collection split across several pages.

## When to use

- Use when a long result set or collection is meaningfully divided into pages.
- Use block-style previous and next links for content pages where destination labels help orientation.

## When not to use

- Do not paginate a short list that is easier to scan on one page.
- Do not use pagination to represent steps in a transaction.

## Anatomy

- **Pagination navigation (required):** A nav landmark has a concise pagination label.
- **Previous and next links:** Directional links use rel=prev or rel=next and hidden “page” context.
- **Page list:** Numbered links include accessible page labels and identify the current page.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Numbered | `nav` | `govuk-pagination` | A results collection where users may move to a particular page. |
| Block previous and next | `nav` | `govuk-pagination`, `govuk-pagination--block` | Sequential content where descriptive previous and next labels help users. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Every destination is a normal server-resolvable link; no GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Omit previous on the first page and next on the last page instead of rendering disabled links.
- Preserve active filters and sorting in pagination URLs.

## Accessibility contract

- Set aria-current="page" on the current page link.
- Give numbered links accessible names such as “Page 3”; hidden context distinguishes Previous page and Next page.
- Hide decorative arrow SVGs using aria-hidden and focusable=false.

## Content rules

- Use “Previous” and “Next” consistently.
- For block navigation, add a concise label that names the destination content.
- Do not show every page number when a large range would become difficult to scan.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.border`

## HTML examples

### Previous and next links

```html
<nav class="govuk-pagination" aria-label="Pagination">
  <div class="govuk-pagination__prev"><a class="govuk-link govuk-pagination__link" href="?page=1" rel="prev"><span class="govuk-pagination__link-title">Previous<span class="govuk-visually-hidden"> page</span></span></a></div>
  <div class="govuk-pagination__next"><a class="govuk-link govuk-pagination__link" href="?page=3" rel="next"><span class="govuk-pagination__link-title">Next<span class="govuk-visually-hidden"> page</span></span></a></div>
</nav>
```
